Science & Technology
• AI-discovered critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggered widespread outages and are being actively exploited, prompting an urgent global patching effort across platforms that rely on PHP (including WordPress-backed sites).
• Research suggests “opt-out” settings on smart TVs may not prevent tracking, raising fresh questions about consumer data privacy.
• Semiconductor advances span from a sapphire-grown film setting a bandgap record to industry debates on scaling beyond transistors, packaging, and computational lithography; Intel marked a delayed Ohio fab milestone.
• NASA highlighted Artemis propulsion progress with an RS‑25 engine test and slated a public Artemis III update, as Mars rover Perseverance set a new off‑world driving record.
Why it matters: Longstanding code underpins much of the internet and infrastructure—when AI uncovers deep flaws, the ripple effects expose systemic risk while accelerating upgrades across cybersecurity, chips, and space systems.

Armed Conflict & Security

• Fighting in Yemen’s Taiz has displaced nearly 260,000 people, while Russia and Ukraine traded strikes despite talk of resuming peace negotiations.
• The U.S. and Israel are developing contingency plans for a potential strike on Iran in early November, NPR reports; Israel was also accused by Syria’s state media of a deadly raid in southern Syria.
• Two European women kidnapped in Niger were freed in Libya; El Salvador’s president launched an operation to rescue Salvadorans kidnapped by gangs in Haiti.
Why it matters: Intensifying flashpoints across the Middle East and persistent conflict in Ukraine add to global security and energy market volatility, with humanitarian costs mounting.

Science & Technology.title: Sapphire-grown semiconductor film sets bandgap record
Science & Technology.text: Semiconductors with wider bandgaps could pave the way for smaller, more efficient electronics that can handle far higher voltages, but the wider this gap becomes, the harder it is to control how well a material conducts electricity. Now, a team led by Darrell Schlom at Cornell University has shown that adding silicon to thin films of aluminum gallium oxide can keep this control intact at bandgaps wider than any semiconductor before it. Their research has been published in Nature.

Science & Technology.title: Algae-powered soft robot arm uses light to grasp and lift small objects
Science & Technology.text: Tiny underwater algae sway gently in the current. All of a sudden, a light shines on them and they form robotlike arms that start to pick up small rocks and put them in floating baskets. Sounds like science fiction, but researchers from Delft University of Technology (the Netherlands) have created a small soft robot arm covered with minuscule algae that can grasp and lift objects. And it's powered by light. This next step in biotechnology has been published in Nature Communications.

This size leaves them with very few natural enemies once they reach adulthood at around eight to 10 years old. But giant manta ray babies, called pups, cannot rely on their size to protect them from predators that live in the open ocean, including several species of shark and orcas.

Science & Technology.title: Manfred “Fred” J. Schindler Is 2027 IEEE President-Elect
Science & Technology.text: IEEE Life Fellow Manfred “Fred” J. Schindler has been elected as the 2027 IEEE president-elect. He will begin serving as president on 1 January 2028.Schindler, who was nominated by the IEEE Board of Directors, received 16,421 votes in the election. Senior Member David Alan Koehler received 13,874 votes.Schindler’s Top 3 Goals as President-ElectStrengthen IEEE’s connection with industry by coordinating events across geography, industry, and technology to revitalize professional activities, especially ones for young professionals.Champion the improvement of IEEE’s digital infrastructure to eliminate manual processes and modernize interfaces.Prioritize the advancement of technology to benefit future generations by expanding and supporting IEEE initiatives and programs.At press time, the results were unofficial until the IEEE Board of Directors accepts the IEEE Teller’s Committee report in November.Schindler, an expert in microwave semiconductor technology, is an independent consultant supporting clients with technical expertise, due diligence, and project management.Throughout his career, he led the development of microwave integrated-circuit technology, from lab demonstrations to high-volume commercial products. He has numerous technical publications and holds 11 patents.Schindler served as CTO of Anlotek, and director of Qorvo and RFMD’s Boston design center. He was applications manager at IBM, engineering manager at ATN Microwave, and a lab manager at Raytheon.An IEEE volunteer for more than 30 years, Schindler served as the 2024 vice president of IEEE Technical Activities and the 2021–2022 Division IV director. He was chair of the IEEE Conferences Committee from 2015 to 2018 and president of the IEEE Microwave Theory and Technology Society (MTTS) in 2003. He received the society’s 2018 Distinguished Service Award and its 2015 N. Walter Cox Award. His award-winning micro-business column has appeared in IEEE Microwave Magazine since 2011.He also led the 2025 One IEEE to Enable Strategic Investments in Innovations and Public Imperative Activities adhoc committee.Schindler is an IEEE–Eta Kappa Nu honorary life member and a MTTS honorary life member.

Society & Human Rights.title: Israel using US-made electroshock weapons on Palestinian detainees | First Thing
Society & Human Rights.text: An American company is still supplying Taser weapons linked to abuse of prisoners by Israeli forces. Plus, 12 valuable lessons about life and death by hospice workersGood morning. An investigation has revealed that Israel is using US-made electroshock weapons on Palestinian detainees. American company Axon is still supplying the Taser weapons despite evidence they have been used to torture prisoners. The news comes as US volunteers including a lawmaker helping Palestinians harvest olives were detained, and Heidi Levine revealed more details of her violent assault by Israeli settlers.Human rights groups have condemned allegations of the repeated torture and ill-treatment of detainees held in Israeli detention centres and prisons using electric shock devices, with Amnesty calling for restrictions on exports of such devices. A spokesperson for the Israel Defense Forces said the abuse of detainees was strictly prohibited.Who was detained by Israel near Nahalin in the occupied West Bank? The Israeli military detained about 80 US, Israeli and British volunteers helping Palestinians harvest olives near Bethlehem, including the New York Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander, several rabbis and Israel’s former deputy attorney general. Soldiers said the area had been declared a closed military zone.What more has Heidi Levine said about the Israeli settler attack on her? The Washington Post photojournalist who was attacked and seriously injured by Israeli settlers on Friday has described how she was saved with the help of local Palestinians. Witnesses said her beating only ceased when young men used slingshots to aim stones at the settlers, forcing them back.What is the latest development with US diplomats in the Middle East? The US state department has ordered some diplomats and the families of US government employees to leave Saudi Arabia, as it faces a barrage of near-daily attacks from Yemen’s Houthis. Reports have emerged of similar US withdrawals in UAE, Jordan, Qatar and Bahrain amid concerns of a return to conflict with Iran after the midterm elections.Where has Elon Musk been spending his election campaign money? Elon Musk’s Super Pac has spent more than $500,000 in New York’s highly competitive 17th congressional district race to help Mike Lawler, the Republican incumbent, hold his seat. Lawler, a moderate Republican, is fending off a challenge from Democrat Cait Conley in one of the most-watched races that could determine who controls Congress.What has happened with letters containing white powder being sent to Congress? Nancy Pelosi’s office received “a suspicious letter” on Wednesday in what appears to be the latest incident of ill-intentioned mailings targeted at US Congress members. The offices of more than three dozen members of Congress across the political spectrum have received envelopes containing white powder in recent days.What is Trump’s polling as the election looms? Donald Trump’s approval rating has sunk to 36%, the lowest recorded, with most respondents expressing frustration over his handling of the US economy, cost of living and Iran war. The president was heckled at least nine times during a campaign event yesterday, and reacted to a supporter punching a demonstrator by saying: “Man, I loved that.” Continue reading...

Entertainment.title: Bose Has Officially Acquired Skullcandy in a Move to Reach a Younger Action Sports Audience
Entertainment.text: SummaryBose announced its official acquisition of competitor Skullcandy on Wednesday, October 21The strategic purchase aims to capture a younger, action-sports-oriented demographic through the established lifestyle brandSkullcandy will continue to operate as a separate brand within the Bose premium consumer audio businessAudio heavyweight Bose has officially announced its official acquisition of competitor Skullcandy. While specific financial details regarding the acquisition were not disclosed, the move signals a strategic shift for the buyer. By absorbing an established lifestyle brand, the historically travel-focused company is actively moving to capture a younger, action-sports-oriented demographic. Rather than dismantling the former rival, Bose confirmed that Skullcandy will continue operating as an entirely separate brand within its premium consumer audio division.Staying true to the lifestyle roots that made it famous, Skullcandy will remain headquartered in Park City, Utah, specifically operating out of the Kimball Junction area. The brand traces its foundation back to a Park City chairlift in 2003, and that mountain-culture DNA is exactly what the new parent company wants to tap into. Moving forward, Bose plans to leverage the distinct product designs of Skullcandy, alongside its deeply rooted relationships with major board sports athletes. Ultimately, the acquisition helps Bose expand its reach to consumers who do not necessarily prioritize active noise cancellation in their daily headphones.Prior to the outright acquisition, the two audio companies engaged in a multiyear partnership that laid the groundwork for this deal. That earlier collaboration integrated the head-tracking spatial audio and active noise cancellation technologies engineered by Bose directly into specific Skullcandy products. Those advanced audio technologies featured in models like the Skullcandy Crusher 1080 ANC headphones and the Method 360 ANC earbuds. According to Bose CEO Lila Snyder, this strategic acquisition aligns with broader efforts by the company to reach more people through a growing portfolio of interconnected brands.This purchase highlights a broader strategy unfolding within Bose as the organization builds out its consumer audio presence. By bringing complementary audio labels into its fold, the company aims to broaden its market presence without altering the core identity of its newly acquired subsidiary.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Shruti Suresh, from the independent watchdog Global Witness, told those in attendance that if they wanted to effect change, they should protest against Jackdaw and the Rosebank oilfield project. Art & Culture.title: YOSHIROTTEN Looks to Outer Space With ‘Transmissions with the Beyond’
Art & Culture.text: SummaryYOSHIROTTEN presents Transmissions with the Beyond  at TOKYO NODE, opening October 30, 2026.The show features JAXA-collaborative space art translating astrophysical data into light and sound.Rooftop activations include a Pokémon TCG 30th-anniversary park and cosmic installations.YOSHIROTTEN is extending his long-running investigation into the unseen beyond Earth with Transmissions with the Beyond, his first large-scale solo exhibition in Tokyo in eight years. Running at TOKYO NODE from October 30, 2026 through January 11, 2027, the exhibition fills approximately 1,500 square meters with the artist’s largest presentation to date of his three principal series - RGB, FUTURE NATURE and SUN - alongside an entirely new body of “space art.”Across a career spanning roughly two decades, YOSHIROTTEN has moved fluidly between fine art, graphic design, music, fashion and spatial design, developing a visual language around what he calls the “Visualization of Things Invisible.” Here, that recurring interest in light, color and nature shifts outward, using the vantage point of TOKYO NODE, around 200 meters above the city, as a departure point for thinking about the cosmos.At the center of the exhibition is a collaboration with the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), translating scientific observation into immersive visual experiences. Developed through conversations with Hiroya Yamaguchi of JAXA’s Institute of Space and Astronautical Science, Puddle Cygnus X-1 transforms observation data from the XRISM mission’s investigation of a black hole into painting and moving image, while "Light Pulse" converts all-sky data captured from the International Space Station into an enveloping installation of light and sound.New works including "Supernova" visualize the explosive life cycle of a star, while Halo renders stellar orbits in sculptural form. The exhibition also brings physical artifacts from Japan’s space program into the gallery, including the solar sail spacecraft IKAROS and the control console used to guide Ohsumi, Japan’s first artificial satellite, into orbit in 1970.Rather than remaining contained within the gallery, Transmissions with the Beyond expands across Toranomon Hills through music, publishing, public art and a Pokémon Trading Card Game collaboration. The rooftop SKY GARDEN & POOL hosts Pokémon Trading Card Game & YOSHIROTTEN Park, building on the artist’s graphics for the game’s 30th anniversary and featuring imagery of Mew, Mewtwo and Pikachu, before transforming after dark into the free BEYOND EARTH GARDEN video installation.Elsewhere, YOSHIROTTEN’s relationship with music feeds into a limited-edition BEYOND EARTH compilation LP, a 100-piece orange km5 Cp2 CD player, a temporary MUSIC BAR UCHU and an accompanying J-WAVE radio program. Together, the projects position the exhibition less as a conventional retrospective than as a multisensory ecosystem where art, science, sound and urban culture intersect, carrying YOSHIROTTEN’s exploration of the invisible from Tokyo toward the scale of outer space.TOKYO NODE GALLERY2-6-2 Toranomon, Minato City,Tokyo, Japan View this post on InstagramClick here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Art & Culture.title: Clive Christian Turns Home Fragrance Into Fine Objects
Art & Culture.text: SummaryClive Christian expands into home fragrance with the Fine Objects collection.Five candles and eight diffusers pair signature scents with sculptural, statement-making vessels.Queen Victoria’s Crown motif reinforces the range’s ornate, heritage-driven design language.Clive Christian wants home fragrance to be seen as much as it is smelled – and its new Fine Objects collection turns candles and diffusers into statement pieces, pushing beyond the discreet vessels that typically recede into an interior.The range draws on the British house’s ornate design language through glossy black, polished metallic and gold-toned finishes, giving each object a more sculptural, almost ceremonial presence. The Crown of Queen Victoria sits prominently across the collection as a recurring visual signature, reinforcing the brand’s heritage while also giving the vessels a recognizable architectural detail of their own.Fine Objects comprises five candles and eight diffusers, each available in two sizes and linked to six of Clive Christian’s Iconic perfumes, using what the house describes as its highest possible concentration of fine perfume oils for home fragrance. Instead than treating scent and object as separate considerations, the collection brings both into the same conversation: fragrance shapes the atmosphere, while the vessel remains part of the room long after the first impression. Artificial Intelligence.title: How Wikipedia’s Editors Keep the Online Encyclopedia Human-Written
Artificial Intelligence.text: Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup, a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia. When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material?Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this.Ellia LebleuEllia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes, part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology.How do editors spot AI-generated writing today?Lebleu: By 2025, the signs of AI writing were becoming subtler and more structural. For example, AI loves the “rule of three,” negative parallelisms, and other structures of speech that aren’t conclusive by themselves but become meaningful as they accumulate. We also look beyond the article. If someone writes five articles of thousands of words each in 5 minutes, there is reason to suspect AI.Does the AI problem just appear in the main text, or also in citations?Lebleu: Fake or misleading citations have become a major worry. Sometimes an AI hallucinates a citation entirely, although that’s much rarer today because of retrieval-augmented generation that allows the AI to find sources. More often, it finds a real source but gets its content completely wrong. AI citations that don’t actually support what is being written are extremely commonplace.English Wikipedia recently prohibited editors from using LLMs to generate articles. How much AI-generated content is still getting through?Lebleu: I’ve been working with [AI-detection company] Pangram to estimate the proportion of AI-generated content. I tested it on Wikipedia content from before ChatGPT and found no false positives, so its results provide a very conservative lower bound. In late 2025, it flagged perhaps 20 percent of new articles and drafts as AI-generated. In early 2026, that went down to 15 or 16 percent. But we don’t yet know whether that’s because our recent policies have had an effect or because models are getting more powerful and Pangram hasn’t had time to adapt.Is Wikipedia using AI to combat AI?Lebleu: Another editor from the project has made an AI source verifier, which goes through the sources on a page and checks whether they match the claims. Since it is itself an AI model, there is no guarantee that it will be correct every time. But if you want something that works at scale and filters out obvious cases, it’s a good first step. The Wikimedia Foundation is also working on a tool called Paste Check, which can flag text pasted directly from some AI chatbots.And we’ve seen Claude sometimes say, “I can’t write a Wikipedia article; it would go against Wikipedia’s policies.” If all major AI companies implemented that kind of prompt refusal, it wouldn’t solve the problem entirely, because there are still open-weight models that can be tweaked to avoid restrictions. But it would help with people who use commercial models and aren’t especially familiar with the technology. Can you tell if the rule prohibiting AI writing is working?Lebleu: It’s still a little early to tell. We see possible effects, such as prompt refusal and the apparent slight drop in AI-generated content. But again, we don’t yet know if that is because models are getting better or because beginners are learning the rules. The vast majority of AI-generated content is submitted by beginner editors, so we’ve made many efforts to make the rule very visible in welcome messages, editing help, and advice. What if AI becomes capable of writing truly reliable Wikipedia articles?Lebleu: That’s one of the big questions we’re facing. When the guideline was passed, it was for very practical reasons: We were flooded with AI content, we didn’t have good tools, and we needed to put a stop to it. But since then, it has taken on a more philosophical dimension. Many people have called Wikipedia “the last good place on the internet.” Being a place that was, in theory, free from AI slop has become part of Wikipedia’s identity.A lot of Wikipedia’s communication is now centered on the idea that we’re a human-written encyclopedia. Even AI companies find that interesting. It can be valuable to have a purely human-written corpus on which to [train] AI systems. The fact that Wikipedia is still that, and will remain that for at least the near future, makes it a precious resource that isn’t replicated anywhere else.But will the people who read and contribute to Wikipedia want it to become partially AI-generated if that makes it more comprehensive? We could preserve Wikipedia’s identity as a human-written corpus while also offering an AI-assisted option.Has Wikipedia reckoned with the idea of “Google Zero”—a possible future in which websites no longer get traffic from Google search?Lebleu: If everything goes through AI search and websites plummet to zero visibility, how do we expose Wikipedia and show that it can be edited and that people can still contribute? Wikipedia is frequently cited in [Google’s] AI Overviews, but users may only see an AI answer citing Wikipedia. They may not realize that Wikipedia is a living project they can edit and contribute to.The Wikimedia Foundation is working on an attribution framework that could give AI users more information about the article [being cited]: when it was last edited, how comprehensive it is, whether editors have flagged problems, and perhaps even a call to action. In the future, readers might even contribute through AI models: “The AI cited Wikipedia, but there seems to be an error. Can I make an edit request and add this other source I found?”I can see a very strong symbiotic relationship between Wikipedia and AI models in the future. I don’t see Wikipedia disappearing, but I can see it taking a very different shape. Yesterday, AI was something to clean up. Today, it’s a tool to help us with the cleanup. Tomorrow, it will be the air we breathe.A condensed version of this article appears in the November 2026 print issue as “Ellia Lebleu.”
